newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. insurance deal activity on record pace in '97.
newsitem.headline: U.S. insurance deal activity on record pace in '97.

text.p: MEXICO CITY, July 17, Reuter - The red-hot U.S. insurance merger market is showing no signs of cooling down, with the volume of deals so far this year ahead of last year's record- setting pace, a U.S. investment banker said.

Gary Parr, head of Morgan Stanley's global insurance group, said there has been about $13 billion worth of insurance deals so far this year, not counting Internationale Nederlanden Groep's agreement earlier this month to acquire Equitable of Iowa for more than $2 billion.
That compares with a total of about $23 billion in deals last year, Parr said in his presentation Wednesday afternoon at the International Insurance Society conference here.
Europe also is running at a record pace this year, following last year's record $39 billion in insurance mergers, he said.
Most of these deals tend to be intra-country combinations such as the Royal Sun Alliance merger last year, he said.
In the United States, the deals this year consisted of about 23 in the property-casualty sector and about nine in the life insurance sector, he said.
Last year, there were about 32 deals in the property-casualty sector, 36 in the life insurance sector and five classified as other.
"The activity continues almost on a weekly basis," Parr said.

"The life insurance industry is undergoing dramatic consolidation and it's primarily driven by an attempt to reach economies of scale. Secondarily, it's an attempt to get better capital utilization," he said.
Most of the buyers of U.S. insurance companies have been other U.S. companies, he said.
Foreign buyers only began to enter the U.S. market in any significant way in 1996, he said.
"The bulk of the activity (in the United States) is domestic consolidation," he said.

However, European insurers are far more aggressive about buying into the U.S. market than U.S. insurers are about buying into the European market, he said, based on an analysis of capital flows on a global basis.
